end.summary: Practised placing BCE dates to the left and CE dates to the right of the timeline midpoint.
end.parentNote: Asha practised ordering BCE and CE dates using a number line and the idea that BCE years count down toward 1 BCE. Aarav correctly explained that 500 BCE is older than 100 BCE and placed CE dates on the right; they also identified checking a source’s claim as a reason historians cross-check. There was still a mix-up about whether zero exists and how 1 BCE relates to the midpoint, and this was not fully corrected by the end. At home, ask Aarav to place 3000 BCE, 500 BCE, 100 BCE, 1 BCE, 1 CE, and 1947 CE on a simple labelled line.
